_comment: Example registry for the auxiliary runner. Two namespaces: `programs` are things that were never MCP tools (they cost zero context before and after; exposing them here makes them callable without making them present), and `servers` are whole MCP servers that used to be wired individually and are now reached as alias.tool. Program ids never contain a dot, so a dotted name is unambiguously server.tool -- no precedence rule needed. Paths use $HOME; the real registry is machine-specific.

regen._note: Simplest useful shape: a choice argument mapped to a command-line switch. `flag` maps the VALUE to the switch, so choices and argv stay in one place.
regen.purpose: Run every documentation generator and report which outputs changed.

mode.help: check reports what would change; write actually writes it.

sync-check._note: Same shape, plus an explicit timeout. A program that shells out to another machine needs longer than the default.
sync-check.purpose: Are the files that exist on BOTH machines actually identical? Compares sha256 of the shared files. A rule nobody can check is a rule that quietly stops being true.

fix.help: yes copies the owner machine's copies over and re-checks.

gpu._note: host is the whole point here. Declared for the GPU box, so calling it from the laptop REFUSES with the ssh command rather than reporting confidently about the wrong machine.
gpu.purpose: What is holding the GPU right now, and how much is free. Run this before any GPU experiment.

memory-engrams._note: Two arguments of different shapes: a choice passed as --op VALUE (no `flag`, so it becomes a --key value pair), and a free-text positional. `optional` means it may be omitted entirely.
memory-engrams.purpose: Embeddings for stored memories: backfill, find near-duplicates, or search by meaning.

op.help: backfill embeds anything new; dupes lists near-identical pairs; similar needs text.

schema-check._note: No arguments at all. `args: {}` is not a placeholder -- it means any argument passed is an error naming what is accepted, rather than a silent no-op.
schema-check.purpose: Does every handler read the arguments its own schema declares? Catches the permanent-silent-null bug.

_servers_comment: Collapsed MCP servers. The runner spawns these on demand, speaks MCP over stdio, calls one tool, and exits. Their tool schemas are NOT carried in context -- ask with op=describe, or let op=find search their live tool lists.

random.purpose: Dice, coin flips, shuffles, samples, UUIDs, weighted choice, normal and uniform draws.

math.purpose: Number theory and algebra: primes, factoring, p-adic valuation, resultants, discriminants, group orbits.

database.purpose: SQLite: connect, query, schema, tables, insert/update/delete, transactions.

projects.purpose: Find projects on disk: locate, list, recent, and per-project info.
